title: Restriction of scalars identifies strict Koszul towers and their units
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\varphi:R\to B$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ a finite list of global sections of $R$, allowing $r=0$. Assume $B$ is flat over $R$, meaning that $B\otimes_R-$ is exact. Use module sheaves and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For $O=R,B$, write $a_{j,R}=a_j$ and $a_{j,B}=\varphi(a_j)$, and define
$$Q_m(O)=\bigotimes_{j=1}^r[O\xrightarrow{a_{j,O}^m}O]\qquad(m\geq1)$$
in degrees $[-r,0]$, using the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Give these the inverse transition $(a_{j,O},1)$ in each two-term factor and the degree-zero maps $O[0]\to Q_m(O)$, as in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system]. For any unbounded $B$-module complex $C$, put $T_B(C)_m=\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_BQ_m(B))$ and $T_R(\operatorname{Res}C)_m=\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Res}C\otimes_RQ_m(R))$.

There is a canonical natural isomorphism of strict towers of complexes
$$\operatorname{Res}T_B(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_R(\operatorname{Res}C).$$
On the summand indexed by any exterior basis element it is the identity on $\operatorname{Res}C$. It commutes with the transition maps and the degree-zero maps from $\operatorname{Res}C$. With $R\lim$ the total right derived inverse limit of strict towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], this induces a natural isomorphism
$$\gamma_C:\operatorname{Res}(R\lim_m T_B(C)_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim_mT_R(\operatorname{Res}C)_m.$$
Writing $\eta_B$ and $\eta_R$ for the units induced by those degree-zero maps, one has $\gamma_C\circ\operatorname{Res}(\eta_B)=\eta_R$. The isomorphism also identifies every derived-limit evaluation with the corresponding restricted evaluation. These comparisons descend to $D(B)$ independently of the representative $C$. For $r=0$ they give the identity under the constant-tower identifications.

source.place: Tag 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul), finite free Koszul model; derived-limit restriction is Tag 0A07 (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), specialized to the identity topos with flat structural ring map. The strict tower, evaluation and unit normalization are made explicit.

proof.text:
Put $[r]=\{1,\ldots,r\}$ and let $e_S$ denote the tensor basis element in $Q_m(O)^{- |S|}$ indexed by $S\subseteq[r]$. The tensor unit maps identify each degree of either tower with $\bigoplus_{S\subseteq[r]}\operatorname{Res}C^{n+|S|}$: on a summand use $c\otimes b\mapsto bc$ over $B$ and $c\otimes x\mapsto\varphi(x)c$ over $R$, with inverses $c\mapsto c\otimes1$. These balanced maps and their inverses commute with restriction to objects of the site, hence define maps of sheaves. Define $h_{C,m}$ to be the identity between these coordinates. For $c\in C^p$ the differential on either side is
$$d(c e_S)=(d_Cc)e_S+\sum_{j\in S}(-1)^{p+\#\{i\in S:i<j\}}\varphi(a_j)^m c\,e_{S\setminus\{j\}}.$$
Indeed this is the ordered tensor differential, and $a_j^m$ acts on $\operatorname{Res}C$ by $\varphi(a_j)^m$. Thus $h_{C,m}$ and its inverse are chain maps. All the sums in each degree have only $2^r$ summands even when $C$ is unbounded.

source.place: Tag 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul), finite free Koszul model; explicit ordered-tensor calculation by the worker.

proof.text: In these coordinates the transition from $m+1$ to $m$ on the $S$-summand is multiplication by $\prod_{j\in S}\varphi(a_j)$ on both sides: a factor contributes $a_j$ precisely when its degree is $-1$. The map from $\operatorname{Res}C$ is its inclusion in the $S=\varnothing$ summand, since each factor uses its degree-zero copy of the ring. Therefore $h_{C,m}$ commutes with transitions and those maps. A chain map $C\to C'$ acts by that same map on every summand, so the $h_{C,m}$ give a natural isomorphism $h_C:\operatorname{Res}^{\rm Tow}T_B(C)\simeq T_R(\operatorname{Res}C)$ of strict coaugmented tower complexes.

source.place: Tag 0913 (lemma-extended-alternating-Cech-is-colimit-koszul), dual transitions and degree-zero maps, as fixed in def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system.

proof.text: Each term of $Q_m(O)$ is a finite sum of copies of $O$. Tensoring with such a term is a finite sum of the identity functor, hence exact. Thus $Q_m(O)$ has flat terms and is bounded above by $0$, so it is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated] with fixed argument $Q_m(O)$: $T_O(-)_m$ preserves every quasi-isomorphism, without a bound on the varying complex. Exactness in the tower category is levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], so kernels, images and cohomology of a complex of towers are evaluated levelwise; consequently $T_O$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms as a functor to complexes of towers. The localization universal property [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] therefore gives $T_O:D(O)\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(O))$. Restriction is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction], applied to the identity geometric morphism with both coefficient maps equal to $\varphi$, both structural isomorphisms identities, and diagram shape either a point or $\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{op}$. It too preserves quasi-isomorphisms, since an exact additive functor preserves the kernels and cokernels computing cohomology. Hence $h$ and the coaugmentations from step 2 descend naturally through localization.

Use the same specialization of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction] to conclude that restriction preserves K-injective complexes of modules and of strict towers. Here flatness is exactly the given exactness of $B\otimes_R-$, and both diagram shapes are small. Also restriction preserves ordinary inverse limits by [lem-weil-pbc-restriction-derived-products]. Concretely a section of either $\operatorname{Res}(\lim_B J)$ or $\lim_R(\operatorname{Res}^{\rm Tow}J)$ is the same compatible family of sections of $J_m$, with the same $R$-action. Thus the canonical comparison is the identity on compatible families; it commutes with every ordinary-limit projection. This applies degree by degree to tower complexes.

source.place: Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), identity underlying topos and structural map R to B; flat restriction supplies a common K-injective model.

proof.text:
Let $X=T_B(C)$ and $Y=T_R(\operatorname{Res}C)$. Apply [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] to the identity underlying topos with source ring $B$, target ring $R$, and structural map $\varphi$. Its direct image is restriction of scalars. Because restriction is exact (step 3), its total derived direct image, also on towers, is represented termwise. The theorem gives a natural isomorphism $a_X:\operatorname{Res}R\lim_B X\simeq R\lim_R\operatorname{Res}^{\rm Tow}X$. Define
$$\gamma_C=R\lim_R(h_C)\circ a_X.$$
For the normalization, choose a K-injective tower resolution $i:X\to J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] and step 4, $\operatorname{Res}^{\rm Tow}i$ is a K-injective resolution of $\operatorname{Res}^{\rm Tow}X$. Thus $a_X$ is represented by the equality $\operatorname{Res}(\lim_B J)=\lim_R(\operatorname{Res}^{\rm Tow}J)$ of step 4, exactly the underived-composite normalization in the cited comparison theorem. This constructs a natural derived comparison before any evaluation and, using step 3, independently of the representative $C$.

source.place: Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), diagram-topos proof; Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), K-injective strict-tower computation.

proof.text:
Write $z_B:\Delta C\to X$ for the strict degree-zero map and $v_B:C\to\lim_BX$ for its ordinary-limit map; the corresponding maps for $Y$ are $z_R,v_R$. By [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system], the unit $\eta_B$ is represented on the resolution $i$ of step 5 by $C\xrightarrow{v_B}\lim_BX\xrightarrow{\lim_Bi}\lim_BJ$. Before applying $h_C$, the restricted unit is therefore the map
$$\operatorname{Res}C\longrightarrow\lim_R\operatorname{Res}^{\rm Tow}X\xrightarrow{\lim_R(\operatorname{Res}^{\rm Tow}i)}\lim_R\operatorname{Res}^{\rm Tow}J.$$
Its first arrow is the ordinary-limit map of $\operatorname{Res}^{\rm Tow}z_B$, since both are the same compatible family. Step 2 says $h_C\operatorname{Res}^{\rm Tow}z_B=z_R$. Naturality of the derived-limit comparison with respect to this strict map now gives $\gamma_C\operatorname{Res}(\eta_B)=\eta_R$. This is equality of the specified derived arrows: both are induced by that same strict coaugmentation followed by the derived-functor comparison, rather than equality inferred only from their evaluations.

source.place: Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), equality of the underived composite direct images; unit convention in def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system.

proof.text:
The comparison $a_X$ commutes with every derived tower projection by [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. Functoriality of total derived inverse limit applied to the strict map $h_C$ then gives, for every $m$,
$$\operatorname{ev}_{R,m}\circ\gamma_C=h_{C,m}\circ\operatorname{Res}(\operatorname{ev}_{B,m}),$$
with the canonical localization and evaluation identifications. Equivalently, in the common resolution of step 5, both projections are induced by the same map $\lim J\to J_m$. This proves the claimed evaluation normalization without asserting that projections determine arbitrary derived arrows.

source.place: Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), evaluation in the diagram-topos proof.

proof.text: If $r=0$, there is only $S=\varnothing$, so $Q_m(O)=O[0]$, $T_O(C)=\Delta C$, $h_C=1$, and the coaugmentation is the identity constant tower. To verify the constant-tower identification, take a K-injective resolution $C\to I$ in module sheaves [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Evaluation at $1$ on towers is exact [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian] and is left adjoint to $\Delta$: a map $V\to\Delta M$ is uniquely its first component $V_1\to M$, the other components being composed with $V_n\to V_1$. Hence $\Delta I$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. Its ordinary inverse limit is $I$, with all projections identity. The total derived limit model [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] therefore identifies $\eta_O$ with $C\to I$, an isomorphism in $D(O)$. Under $R\lim\Delta C\cong C$, the unit is identity. The unit equation in step 6 forces $\gamma_C$ to be identity under these identifications, as required.
